_comment: Hand-curated layer of docs/capabilities.json (capability-config.md §2 p.3). The emitter (stapel_profiles/_capabilities.py) merges this over the derived axes; an axis present in conf.py DEFAULTS but missing here (or vice versa) is a loud emission error. Keep business_label/summary in business language — they surface in CTO conversations, not in code. surface_roots/surface are the third section (stapel_tools.surface): the symbols a product is meant to CALL rather than reimplement. The roots select the symbols; every selected symbol MUST carry an intent line here or emission fails naming it, and an intent for a symbol no root selects fails as stale prose. Most of this module's value is HTTP + comm events, so the roots are deliberately narrow — actions.py (bus subscribers, invoked by delivery, never by a caller) and the codegen shims are not surface.
provides: User profiles and social graph: display name, avatar, locale/currency/measurement preferences, notification opt-outs, and follow/unfollow/block relationships between users, with a relationship-status lookup.

requires.reason: comm bus (events/functions), JWT authentication, GDPR provider registry, AppSettings config layer
consumes the user.registered / user.deleted comm events (OAuth avatar import, GDPR erasure on account deletion) that stapel-auth emits; decoupled via the comm bus, not a hard import dependency
avatar storage/existence checks (PROFILES_AVATAR_CHECK=comm calls cdn.media_exists) and OAuth avatar import (cdn.import_from_url) go through stapel_core.comm to a CDN provider
surfaces this module's registered GDPR provider (profile section export/erase) through DSR endpoints; the registration itself only needs stapel-core.gdpr

extension_points.name: serializer_seams
extension_points.summary: Every profile/relationship view declares request/response serializer seams (SerializerSeamsMixin) — subclass the view, override the attribute, remount the URL; keep calling super() in serializer overrides so profile.changed keeps publishing.

extension_points.name: profile_extras_relation
extension_points.summary: Extend the profile without a fork: an app-layer model with a OneToOne to profiles.Profile (or keyed by the same user_id UUID), exposed through the serializer seams — models here are deliberately not swappable.

extension_points.name: profile.changed
extension_points.summary: The primary hook for syncing derived data: emitted on every profile mutation (keyed by user_id) — subscribe with @on_action from any module or the host app, no import of this package.

PROFILES_AVATAR_CHECK.summary: Controls how the profile service confirms an uploaded avatar reference actually exists on the CDN before saving it: through the internal comm bus (default) or skipped entirely (only the reference format is still validated).

get_profile_model.intent: THE way to reach the profile DAO: resolves STAPEL_SWAP["PROFILES_PROFILE_MODEL"], so a host that assembled its own extended Profile (build_profile_model) is honoured. Views, serializers, admin, GDPR providers and product code all go through it — a direct `from stapel_profiles.models import Profile` pins the zero-field default and silently ignores the swap, which is exactly what the SWAP001 lint flags.

validate_avatar_reference.intent: Format-check an avatar value against its declared avatar_source before storing it — the source taxonomy (file/url/gravatar/cdn) lives here, and only `cdn` has a fixed `avatar/<64-hex>` wire shape. Reach for it from any serializer seam that accepts an avatar; validating with the core CDN checker directly instead rejects every non-CDN source a project is allowed to pick.

is_cdn_avatar_reference.intent: Answer whether an avatar value IS a stapel-cdn reference (`avatar/<64-hex>`) — the single discriminator behind the avatar/avatar_source pair invariant. Reach for it when you have a ref and need to know where it came from; matching the prefix or the slash by hand is how a `product/<hash>` ref or a path-like upload key gets mistaken for a CDN avatar.

resolve_avatar_source.intent: The avatar_source that MUST accompany a given avatar value — returns the declared source unchanged unless the value is unmistakably a CDN ref tagged otherwise. Call it in any writer that sets an avatar outside this module's serializers; storing the ref and letting the model default choose the tag is exactly how a live stand ended up serving 500s from a cosmetic avatar.

build_profile_model.intent: Assemble a project's extended, swappable Profile subclass from a field manifest (identity preset + standard fields + custom ProfileFieldDefs) — call it once in your OWN app's models.py and point STAPEL_SWAP["PROFILES_PROFILE_MODEL"] at the result, so the extra columns and their migration live in the project rather than in this package.

assemble_profile_fields.intent: The manifest → {field_name: Django field} primitive under build_profile_model, failing loudly at assembly time on an unknown identity preset or standard-field name instead of with a confusing system check later. Call it directly only when splicing profile fields into a model you already own; if you want a Profile, call build_profile_model.

validate_display_name.intent: This module's display-name canon — minimum length, control/invisible characters and emoji, raising StapelValidationError with the module's own error keys so the frontend gets a translatable key rather than a sentence. Any host onboarding form, admin action or importer that writes a name must run it through here instead of inventing a second, differently-strict regex; the user.registered pre-fill already does.

validate_avatar_url.intent: The import half of the avatar URL boundary: refuses an external avatar whose scheme this deployment does not accept (https only by default) or whose host is outside PROFILES_AVATAR_URL_ALLOWED_HOSTS. Any writer that stores an avatar without passing through this module's serializer must call it, or a user-controlled active-scheme string reaches every consumer that renders a profile.

is_safe_avatar_url.intent: The read half of the same boundary, as a predicate: whether a stored avatar URL may still be handed to a client. Use it before rendering an avatar reference that did not come from this module's serializers — an old row is not evidence that today's policy allows it.

avatar_url_allowed_schemes.intent: The schemes this deployment accepts for external avatars (PROFILES_AVATAR_URL_ALLOWED_SCHEMES, normalized). Read the policy from here rather than hardcoding "https" in a second place that will not follow when a host changes it.

avatar_url_allowed_hosts.intent: The external avatar host allowlist (PROFILES_AVATAR_URL_ALLOWED_HOSTS, normalized; empty = any host). Same reason as the schemes accessor: one reading of the policy, not two.

validate_gravatar_hash.intent: Refuse a gravatar avatar that is not an email hash. The value is interpolated into a gravatar URL, so a 'hash' carrying a path or a query is an arbitrary destination wearing a hash's name.

is_gravatar_hash.intent: Predicate form of the gravatar rule, for read paths deciding whether a stored value may be turned into a URL.

publish_profile_changed.intent: Emit profile.changed for a mutated profile row — the payload shape (schemas/emits/profile.changed.json) and the best-effort savepoint isolation that keeps a broker failure from 500-ing the request both live inside. Call it after ANY profile write that does not go through this module's serializers (a data migration, an admin action, a product's own service function), or every downstream consumer of the event quietly desyncs.

avatar_image.intent: The renderable StapelImage for a profile's avatar — variant ladder plus blur-up — mapping this module's avatar_source taxonomy onto the matching media provider. A custom profile presenter or serializer seam must call this rather than hand the raw ref to the media builder with a guessed provider: a pil-default deployment describing CDN refs is how meettoday shipped an empty variant ladder.

declared_languages.intent: Answer which languages this deployment actually DECLARED (it set LANGUAGES itself), as {code: name} — Django's 100-entry default answers {} because nobody claimed it. Reach for it wherever a language code must be validated or offered; reading settings.LANGUAGES directly cannot tell a declaration from Django's default and turns an unconfigured project into one that claims a hundred languages.

ensure_declared_languages.intent: Make the Language reference table agree with the declaration: materialise a row for every declared code that has none. Reach for it before listing or validating languages in a deployment that never ran `sync_languages` — without it the picker is empty and every app_language write 400s, so no user can ever state a language and every notification downstream has to guess at its recipient's.
